title: Disk Full — But Deleting the Log Didn't Free Any Space
intro: The app server's root disk hit 100%, writes are failing. A teammate already deleted the huge /var/log/app/debug.log file — but df still shows the disk full.

steps.fake_output:
Filesystem      Size  Used  Avail  Use%  Mounted on
/dev/sda1        50G   50G     0   100%  /
steps.hint: Start by confirming the symptom, even when someone already told you what it is.

steps.prompt: Check what's actually using space under /var/log now that the file is deleted.
steps.hint: du adds up the sizes of files it can SEE in the directory tree.

steps.prompt: du shows almost nothing, but df says the disk is full. The space must belong to a file that was deleted but is still held open by a running process. Find deleted-but-open files.
steps.fake_output:
COMMAND  PID   USER    FD  TYPE  SIZE/OFF      NLINK  NAME
node    4821  appsvc  12w  REG   41203847168   0     /var/log/app/debug.log (deleted)
steps.hint: lsof +L1 lists open files with a link count of 0 — i.e. deleted from the directory, but still open.

steps.prompt: The app (PID 4821) still has the deleted 41GB file open, so the kernel can't free the space. Restart the service so it releases the file handle.
steps.hint: Once the process closes its handle, the space is released immediately.

steps.fake_output:
Filesystem      Size  Used  Avail  Use%  Mounted on
/dev/sda1        50G    9G   41G    18%   /

resolution: Deleting a file on Linux only removes its directory entry — the actual disk blocks are freed only once no process has it open. The app was still writing to its (now-deleted) 41GB debug log, so df (which reports actual block usage) kept showing 100% while du (which walks visible files) showed almost nothing. That df/du mismatch is the telltale sign of this exact problem. Restarting the app released the handle and freed the space. If a restart isn't acceptable, truncating instead of deleting ('> /var/log/app/debug.log' or 'truncate -s 0') frees the space while the file stays open. The real fixes: turn off debug logging in production, and configure logrotate (with copytruncate, or a signal telling the app to reopen its log) so no log file grows unbounded again.
